The Third and Fourth Derivatives of the Jeffreys Penalty

Source: R/jfp_outer.R
jfp_deriv3_dir.Rd

jfp_deriv3_dir() returns the derivative of the Hessian of \(\sum_b a_b\log|\tilde I_b|\) along a direction \(v\) of the joint vector, and jfp_deriv4_dir() its second derivative along two directions \(v\) and \(w\), as matrices over the joint vector. jfp_deriv3() and jfp_deriv4() return their traces against a symmetric matrix \(M\), without assembling them.

Usage

jfp_deriv3_dir(st, v)

jfp_deriv3(st, M, v)

jfp_deriv4_dir(st, v, w)

jfp_deriv4(st, M, v, w)

Arguments

st

A state, from jfp_state().

v, w

Directions over the joint vector.

M

A symmetric matrix over the joint vector.

Value

jfp_deriv3_dir() and jfp_deriv4_dir() a base matrix over the joint vector; jfp_deriv3() and jfp_deriv4() a single number.

Details

The derivatives are those of the determinant with the derivatives of the family's expected information to the fourth order, from distributions7::distrib_dexpected_hessian() and its siblings of orders two to four. A term with both indices inside one derivative of the block's matrix is a weighted cross product of the designs and has the sparsity of the information; the others are products of low rank through matrices of \(\tilde p^2\) columns. They are written for blocks whose rows do not move, in a model without a filter and without a term whose block is recomputed at the coefficients, and they signal an error elsewhere.

The outer criterion reads them: the derivative of its penalized matrix along the movement of the mode carries \(-a\,D_3(v)\), and its second derivative \(-a\,D_4(v, w)\) (statmod_penalty_dbeta(), statmod_penalty_second()).
